text: The difference composition FAILS TO OPEN before an active account exists: `ScopeNotSupportedYet { scope: "ListMembers-active-mute-no-active-account" }` (nip51_sources.rs:130-132, mute source is RequireActive). Plain follows opens fine pre-login (AllowMissingActive) and just shows empty. So the Rust shells that open the home feed with the difference scope get a hard open-error if they open before sign-in, whereas iOS/plain-follows degrades gracefully. This is a Chirp-composition fragility, not the empty-feed symptom (the device DID open + emit a snapshot). [...] **The device empty-feed is a device-side test-harness issue, not a framework bug.** The 0-item snapshot was the initial empty-window frame; the events reached the wire (raw-websocket verified) but almost certainly never reached kernel ingest — most likely the `nak`-seeded notes failing signature verification (which the raw-websocket check doesn't exercise), or a subscription-routing mismatch. That's why both platforms saw it. I've updated chirp#39/#40 with the verdict and the precise next step (instrument whether `notify_event_observers` fires for the seeded events on device), and filed one real secondary NMP finding (#2930: the "follows minus mutes" scope hard-errors pre-login where plain follows degrades gracefully — an ergonomics gap).
